question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in agent self-continuation system, including model-controlled delegate scheduling, volitional compaction requests, cross-session targeting, and new config/protocol/SDK surfaces?
rationale: The branch is not a narrow repair: it creates a new core agent lifecycle mode and security-sensitive routing surface that automation cannot approve from tests alone.

options.title: Accept After Sign-Off And Proof
options.body: Approve the core direction only after conflict resolution, maintainer product/security review, and exact-head live proof for all lifecycle and boundary paths.

options.title: Narrow To Same-Session Continuation
options.body: Require a smaller branch that keeps continuation same-session only and defers cross-session targeting, fanout-all, and broader SDK/protocol exposure.

options.title: Defer To Design Issue
options.body: Pause or close the PR as implementation-first until a canonical design issue fixes the permanent product contract.

recommendation.title: Accept After Sign-Off And Proof
recommendation.body: Approve the core direction only after conflict resolution, maintainer product/security review, and exact-head live proof for all lifecycle and boundary paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history points to steipete across the adjacent session, reply, TaskFlow, and protocol surfaces, making this the best available routing owner.
